question: Which private-equity rivals are most active in our sectors?
html:
The most active rivals are concentrated in residential services, where Sila (Goldman Sachs), Legacy/HL Bowman (Gridiron), Ally (Watchtower) and Northwinds (TruArc) are buying near Punctual Pros. Electrical rivals Kohlberg and Huron are active but mostly outside CET's New England footprint, and Frontline and Thomas Scientific face fewer direct copies.

Activity by sector

Sector (portfolio company)Most active rivalsPressure on BSP
Residential HVAC/plumbing (Punctual Pros)Apex/Alpine, Wrench/LGP, TurnPoint/OMERS, Redwood/Altas, Any Hour/Knox Lane, T3/Riverside. In PA/NJ: Sila, Legacy/HL Bowman, Ally, NorthwindsHighest
Commercial electrical (CET)Kohlberg (RESA Power, Loenbro, CLEAResult), Huron (Criticore, Albireo). IES is a public strategic buyerModerate, rising
Legal IT and billing (Frontline)Alpine's Evergreen, EagleTree/Integreon, BVLow for now
Lab distribution (Thomas Scientific)Calibre ScientificFocused, one main rival

(Private-equity landscape)

Residential services

  • National consolidators set add-on pricing (Private-equity landscape).
  • Lenders favor scale. Wrench, Apex, Redwood and Legacy borrow at S+425–475, marked at par. TurnPoint, Horizon, Any Hour and Len the Plumber pay part PIK interest and are marked at 89–94 (Competitor filings).
  • Sila is the healthiest local buyer. Revenue is est. $450–650M (low confidence), and nearly all of its growth has come from acquisitions (Competitor filings).
  • Horizon (≥$211M first lien at Blue Owl, marked 92.5) and Heartland (debt maturing Dec 15, 2026) are more likely to sell assets or restructure than to bid (Competitor filings).

Electrical and energy services

  • PE has driven most electrical-contractor M&A since 2023 (Private-equity landscape).
  • Albireo's Upstate NY expansion and Kohlberg's energy-efficiency cluster are the closest threats to New England.
  • IES has no net debt and earns 11.4% operating margins. It can pay strategic prices for New England contractors (Competitor filings).

Fund-level peers

  • BSP's Fund I is about $335M (Form D). Key rivals run $0.9–2.1B flagships: Trivest VII, Bertram V and Gridiron V.
  • The closest peers by thesis are MidOcean, CIVC, Trilantic North America, Palladium, Vesterra/Comvest and Bertram (Private-equity landscape).
  • BSP's $50–250M check range is unverified (BSP firm profile).

Gaps

  • The context has no rival-activity data for Bully Pulpit International or Fair Harbor. Deal-count data by sponsor for public affairs and DTC apparel would close this gap.
  • Some fund sizes are unknown because the research hit a search-quota limit. These include Gryphon VI, Trilantic VII and Palladium VI (Private-equity landscape).

Next actions

  • Build a proprietary outreach list of PA/NJ shops below $3M EBITDA for Punctual Pros. Watch Horizon and Heartland for asset sales before Dec 15, 2026.
  • Speed up CET's New England add-on cadence. Track Albireo and Kohlberg entries into the region monthly.
  • Lock in law-firm MSP and billing add-ons for Frontline before a generalist MSP builds a legal vertical.
  • Commission a competitor scan for Bully Pulpit International and Fair Harbor, and fill the missing fund sizes.
